title: KV cache as an admission budget
caption: The book’s long-context admission example: an eight-H100 node serving a 70B-class GQA model reserves 141.2 GB for FP16 weights and 20 GB for system state, leaving a 526 GB KV pool. Each 128K-token request costs 42.9 GB at 327,680 bytes per token, so twelve such requests exhaust the pool.
alt: Memory budget on an eight-H100 node showing weights, reserve, a 526 GB KV pool, and twelve 128K-token requests filling that pool

title: Admission moves to the iteration boundary
caption: Static membership pads completed rows until the longest sequence finishes; continuous batching admits replacement work into freed slots at iteration boundaries, subject to queueing, KV capacity and prefill scheduling.
alt: Rows of sequence work showing idle padding in static batching and replacement work filling those slots in continuous batching

title: Prefill and decode lanes
caption: Prefill is one wide compute-bound pass that sets TTFT; decode is a serial chain of bandwidth-bound steps that sets TPOT. Disaggregation scales them independently but pays queueing plus the alpha-plus-bytes-over-beta KV handoff.
alt: Wide prefill block handing a KV cache to many narrow decode steps

title: Fan-out inherits the slowest leaf
caption: With 100 independent leaves that are each slow one percent of the time, about 63 percent of requests meet at least one slow leaf. Holding request-level p99 pushes each leaf toward roughly p99.99.
alt: One request fanning out to many leaves, with the slowest leaf controlling completion
